lives_at.note: Andreas puts him in one of the 'small log buildings' near the agency house at the foot of State Street, alongside Billy Caldwell. Those buildings are not in data/structures/ and the list they come from describes the settlement before the town, so there is nothing to link to and nothing to date.

works_at.note: The government blacksmith shop of the agency establishment, which is what this structure record IS. THE PARCEL'S BEST NEW OCCUPANT LINK: a building that had nobody in it now has the man the treaty paid for.

present_on_scene_date.note: THE AGENCY ITSELF IS THE PROBLEM. Andreas's list of the establishment is written for the period of Owen's agency generally and not for 1835, and the treaty obligation that created the post was superseded by the cession of 1833. Whether a government smith for the Potawatomi was still at his anvil on 1 July 1835, six weeks before the removal, is not stated anywhere reached, and the value says so.

persons.name: David McKee

occupation.note: Government blacksmith to the Indian agency at Chicago. Andreas names the agency establishment under Col. Owen: sub-agents Kercheval and Stuart, 'Billy Caldwell (Sauganash) as interpreter; David McKee as blacksmith, and Joseph Porthier as striker'. The 1821 treaty obliged the United States to keep a blacksmith at Chicago for the Potawatomi and McKee was hired for that.

persons.note: HE IS THE NAMED OCCUPANT THIS DATASET'S GOVERNMENT SMITHY HAS BEEN MISSING. data/structures/blacksmith_shop_state_st.json describes 'a building known only as a clause in other people's sentences' with an empty occupants field; McKee is the man in the clause. Andreas's list of the settlement's residents puts 'small log buildings occupied by the blacksmith, Mr. McKee, and Billy Caldwell' in the vicinity of Cobweb Castle, and he signed the 1832 militia agreement. OLD SETTLERS, 1882 — A DATE OF DEATH, AND NOTHING ABOUT 1835. John Wentworth's roll of old settlers who had died since 1 January 1881, kept for the Calumet Club and printed in the Chicago Tribune of 25 April 1882, carries “David McKee, April 9, 1881.”. That corroborates a Chicago residence before 1840 and fixes the END of this life, which this record did not carry; it is not an arrival and it places nobody in the town on 1 July 1835. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a later recollection corroborates, enriches and dates and cannot lift a rung by itself, so this record's GRADE IS UNCHANGED by it: T-0513 consolidates the identity and T-0515 regrades. Identity by rule OS1 — surname and spelled-out forename agree, one bearer (data/research/old_settlers/crosswalk.json).

resident_research.evidence_for: Early Chicago histories independently identify David McKee as the government/agency blacksmith near the foot of State Street. The occupation and institutional role are distinctive enough to corroborate the resident record, while the exact July 1835 workplace continuity is not extended beyond the sources.

research_note: THE MAN THE 1821 TREATY PAID TO SHOE POTAWATOMI HORSES, AT AN ANVIL THIS PROJECT MODELS. This household exists to close a loop the structures layer left open, and the presence field is where the honesty is: the shop is in the scene and the smith may not have been. STANDING CONSTRAINT. AGENTS.md: the final removal of the Potawatomi from Chicago occurred in August 1835, inside this project's first target year and six weeks AFTER the scene date; Native presence, representation and depiction are not research gaps to be filled by inference, and v1 ships no human figures at all. This record is a dataset entry that states what named sources say about a named person and adds nothing. It carries review_required so that no scene containing it can be marked released before the consultation the project has committed to.

directories.note: LATER EVIDENCE, BESIDE THE 1835 CLAIMS AND NOT INSIDE THEM. A Chicago directory of 1839, 1843 or 1844 meets somebody of this name and this pass records what it prints. Under the ratified ladder a directory read after 1835 can corroborate that a person attested here was still in Chicago and can print a trade or a street the 1835 record never had; on its own it makes nobody a resident of 1835. Nothing on this person's 1835 record was regraded, moved, dated or given an occupation by this entry.
